questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que significa 'abolição' quando falamos da história do Brasil?
questions.answer: O fim da escravidão
questions.hint: Pense no tema das leis estudadas nesta semana.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano foi assinada a Lei Áurea?
questions.hint: Foi um ano antes da Proclamação da República.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas leis foi a primeira a ser aprovada?
questions.answer: Lei Eusébio de Queirós
questions.hint: Ela é do meio do século XIX, anos antes das outras.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que a Lei Eusébio de Queirós (1850) proibiu?
options: O tráfico de africanos escravizados para o Brasil
A escravidão em todo o Brasil
A venda de terras para imigrantes
questions.answer: O tráfico de africanos escravizados para o Brasil
questions.hint: Ela atacou a chegada de novas pessoas escravizadas pelo oceano.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual país pressionou fortemente o Brasil a acabar com o tráfico negreiro no século XIX?
questions.answer: Inglaterra
questions.hint: Era a maior potência naval e industrial da época.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual lei, de 1871, declarou livres os filhos de mulheres escravizadas nascidos a partir daquela data?
questions.answer: Lei do Ventre Livre
questions.hint: O nome da lei fala do lugar onde o bebê é gerado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que a Lei do Ventre Livre teve efeito limitado no começo?
options: As crianças podiam continuar sob o controle do senhor até os 21 anos
Ela só valia para a cidade do Rio de Janeiro
Ela foi anulada no ano seguinte
questions.answer: As crianças podiam continuar sob o controle do senhor até os 21 anos
questions.hint: Pense em quem ficava cuidando — e se beneficiando do trabalho — das crianças.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual lei de 1885 libertava as pessoas escravizadas com 60 anos ou mais?
questions.answer: Lei dos Sexagenários
questions.hint: O nome da lei vem da palavra para quem tem sessenta anos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que muitos abolicionistas criticaram a Lei dos Sexagenários?
options: Poucos escravizados chegavam aos 60 anos e ainda deviam trabalhar mais alguns anos
Ela libertava todos de uma vez
Ela obrigava o governo a pagar salários
questions.answer: Poucos escravizados chegavam aos 60 anos e ainda deviam trabalhar mais alguns anos
questions.hint: Pense nas condições de vida e na expectativa de vida dos escravizados.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A Lei Eusébio de Queirós é de 1850 e a Lei Áurea é de 1888. Quantos anos se passaram entre elas?
questions.hint: Faça a subtração entre os dois anos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem assinou a Lei Áurea em 13 de maio de 1888?
questions.answer: A princesa Isabel
questions.hint: Ela governava como regente, pois o imperador estava fora do país.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual característica marcou a Lei Áurea?
options: Era curta e extinguia a escravidão sem indenizar os senhores
Libertava a escravidão aos poucos, em dez anos
Garantia terras a todos os libertos
questions.answer: Era curta e extinguia a escravidão sem indenizar os senhores
questions.hint: Ela tinha só dois artigos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual província brasileira aboliu a escravidão em 1884, antes da Lei Áurea?
questions.answer: Ceará
questions.hint: Fica no Nordeste e ficou conhecida como 'Terra da Luz'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que se diz que as leis abolicionistas anteriores à Lei Áurea foram 'graduais'?
options: Elas acabavam com a escravidão aos poucos, protegendo os interesses dos senhores
Elas foram feitas pelos próprios escravizados
Elas eram leis de outros países
questions.answer: Elas acabavam com a escravidão aos poucos, protegendo os interesses dos senhores
questions.hint: Compare o efeito de cada lei com a Lei Áurea.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que a abolição de 1888 não garantiu, por si só, uma vida digna aos libertos.
questions.hint: Pense em terra, trabalho, educação e direitos depois de 13 de maio.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Além das leis, que outros fatores ajudaram a enfraquecer a escravidão no Brasil nas décadas de 1870 e 1880?
questions.hint: Lembre-se das fugas, dos quilombos e do movimento abolicionista.

comp.topic: CPU performance: clock speed, cores and cache

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does the clock speed of a CPU measure?
options: The number of instruction cycles it can carry out per second
The amount of data it can store
questions.answer: The number of instruction cycles it can carry out per second
questions.hint: Think about ticks per second.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In which unit is CPU clock speed usually given?
questions.answer: Gigahertz (GHz)
questions.hint: Hertz means 'per second'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A CPU runs at 3 GHz. How many billion cycles does it carry out each second?
questions.hint: 1 GHz is one billion cycles per second.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A CPU has a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. How many cycles per second is that? Give the full number.
questions.hint: Multiply by one billion.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is a CPU core?
options: A processing unit that can fetch, decode and execute instructions independently
The fan that cools the processor
A cable connecting the CPU to memory
questions.answer: A processing unit that can fetch, decode and execute instructions independently
questions.hint: A multi-core CPU contains several of these.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How many cores does a quad-core processor have? Write the number in words.
questions.answer: four
questions.hint: 'Quad' appears in words like quadrilateral.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why does doubling the number of cores not always double performance?
options: Some programs cannot be split into tasks that run at the same time
Cores slow each other down by sharing a fan
Extra cores reduce the clock speed to zero
The operating system ignores extra cores
questions.answer: Some programs cannot be split into tasks that run at the same time
questions.hint: Think about whether every task can be shared between workers.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is cache memory?
options: A small, very fast memory close to the CPU that stores frequently used data and instructions
A large, slow storage device for files
Memory used only by the graphics card
A backup copy of the hard drive
questions.answer: A small, very fast memory close to the CPU that stores frequently used data and instructions
questions.hint: It saves the CPU from going to RAM so often.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why does a larger cache usually improve CPU performance?
options: More data can be fetched quickly without accessing slower RAM
questions.answer: More data can be fetched quickly without accessing slower RAM
questions.hint: Compare the speed of cache and RAM.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which level of cache is usually the smallest and fastest?
questions.answer: L1
questions.hint: It is closest to each core.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement about cache is correct?
options: Cache is faster but more expensive per byte than RAM
Cache keeps data when the power is off
questions.answer: Cache is faster but more expensive per byte than RAM
questions.hint: That is why computers do not have huge caches.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which repeating three-stage cycle does each CPU core carry out? (three words, joined by hyphens)
questions.answer: fetch-decode-execute
questions.hint: The first stage collects an instruction from memory.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is a disadvantage of increasing clock speed by overclocking?
options: The CPU produces more heat and may become unstable
The computer loses its operating system
questions.answer: The CPU produces more heat and may become unstable
questions.hint: Think about what happens to components that work harder.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: CPU A: 3.0 GHz, 4 cores, 8 MB cache. CPU B: 3.0 GHz, 8 cores, 16 MB cache. Which is likely to perform better on multi-threaded tasks such as video editing?
options: It is impossible for either to run video editing
questions.answer: CPU B
questions.hint: Compare the factors that differ.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A student says: 'A 4 GHz single-core CPU is always faster than a 3 GHz quad-core CPU.' Explain why this is not always true.
questions.hint: Consider what kind of program is running.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain how clock speed, number of cores and cache size each affect the performance of a CPU.
questions.hint: Write about each factor in turn.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In an IGCSE summary task, what should you mainly do?
options: Select the relevant points and express them concisely
Give your opinion on the topic
Add new examples of your own
questions.answer: Select the relevant points and express them concisely
questions.hint: Think about what 'relevant' and 'concise' mean.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does 'concise' mean in summary writing?
options: Using few words while keeping the meaning
questions.answer: Using few words while keeping the meaning
questions.hint: The opposite of wordy.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What should you do first when preparing a summary?
options: Read the question carefully to find exactly what to focus on
Start writing the final version at once
Count the words in the passage
questions.answer: Read the question carefully to find exactly what to focus on
questions.hint: The focus of the task decides which points count.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these should usually be left out of a summary?
options: Main ideas linked to the question
Key facts relevant to the task
Important reasons given in the text
questions.answer: Examples, anecdotes and repetition
questions.hint: Ask yourself whether the detail adds a new point.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why are you asked to use your 'own words' in a summary?
options: To show you have understood the ideas
To avoid using any key terms at all
questions.answer: To show you have understood the ideas
questions.hint: Copying does not prove understanding.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Passage: 'Bees pollinate crops, which helps farmers grow food. Some bees, like the one I saw last summer, are bright yellow.' Task: the importance of bees. Which point is relevant?
options: Bees pollinate crops that farmers grow
The writer saw a bee last summer
Bees can be seen in summer
questions.answer: Bees pollinate crops that farmers grow
questions.hint: Which detail answers the task?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which version is the most concise way to express: 'At this present moment in time, a large number of people are increasingly choosing to cycle to work'?
options: More people are now cycling to work.
At this moment, a large number of people choose to cycle.
People, at present, are increasingly choosing, in large numbers, to cycle.
In this time, many, many people cycle to work now.
questions.answer: More people are now cycling to work.
questions.hint: Remove every word that adds no meaning.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word could replace the list 'apples, oranges, bananas and grapes' in a summary?
questions.answer: fruit
questions.hint: Find the general category.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is meant by 'fluency' in summary writing?
options: Writing in clear, connected sentences that read smoothly
Using as many quotations as possible
questions.answer: Writing in clear, connected sentences that read smoothly
questions.hint: Think about how the sentences link to one another.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which connective best links two similar points in a summary?
questions.answer: Furthermore
questions.hint: Which word adds rather than contrasts?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which connective best introduces a contrasting point?
questions.answer: However
questions.hint: Look for the word that signals a change of direction.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A summary has a word limit of 120 words. What is the best approach?
options: Stay within the limit and cover as many relevant points as possible
Ignore the limit if the points are good
questions.answer: Stay within the limit and cover as many relevant points as possible
questions.hint: Examiners reward relevance and concision.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Should you include your own opinion in an IGCSE summary?
options: No, only the ideas from the passage
Only if you disagree with the writer
questions.answer: No, only the ideas from the passage
questions.hint: A summary reports, it does not argue.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence combines these two points most fluently? 'Plastic harms sea animals.' 'Plastic takes centuries to break down.'
options: Plastic harms sea animals and takes centuries to break down.
Plastic harms sea animals. Plastic takes centuries. To break down.
Plastic, sea animals, centuries, break down.
Sea animals are harmed by plastic, plastic which takes centuries, to break down it.
questions.answer: Plastic harms sea animals and takes centuries to break down.
questions.hint: Avoid repeating the subject.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain why highlighting key points before writing can improve a summary.
questions.hint: Think about selection and organisation.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain the difference between a summary and a retelling of a text.
questions.hint: Consider length, focus and what is left out.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Approximately when was Macbeth first performed?
questions.answer: Around 1606
questions.hint: It was written during the reign of the first Stuart king of England.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which king was on the English throne when Macbeth was written?
questions.answer: James I
questions.hint: He was also King of Scotland.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why might the theme of witchcraft have interested King James?
options: He had written a book about witches and believed in their power
He was a witch-hunter in France
questions.answer: He had written a book about witches and believed in their power
questions.hint: His book was called Daemonologie.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What did the 'divine right of kings' mean to Jacobean audiences?
options: Kings were chosen by God, so killing a king was a terrible sin
Kings were elected by the people
Anyone could become king by fighting
questions.answer: Kings were chosen by God, so killing a king was a terrible sin
questions.hint: Think about who gives a king his authority.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which event of 1605 made the killing of a king a sensitive topic?
questions.answer: The Gunpowder Plot
questions.hint: Plotters planned to blow up Parliament.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What name do the witches give themselves in the play? (two words)
questions.answer: weird sisters
questions.hint: The first word once meant 'fate'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How does the play open in Act 1 Scene 1?
options: With the witches meeting in thunder and lightning
With a feast at the castle
questions.answer: With the witches meeting in thunder and lightning
questions.hint: The atmosphere is set straight away.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the effect of opening the play with the witches?
options: It creates a supernatural, threatening mood from the start
It makes the play feel like a comedy
It introduces Macbeth as a villain
It explains the history of Scotland
questions.answer: It creates a supernatural, threatening mood from the start
questions.hint: Think about the first impression on the audience.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the meaning of 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair'?
options: Appearances can be deceptive; good and evil are confused
questions.answer: Appearances can be deceptive; good and evil are confused
questions.hint: This idea of opposites returns throughout the play.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which three titles do the witches use to greet Macbeth?
options: Thane of Glamis, Thane of Cawdor, king hereafter
Lord of Fife, Earl of York, prince of Wales
Duke of Glamis, King of England, Thane of Ross
Thane of Fife, King of Norway, Lord Cawdor
questions.answer: Thane of Glamis, Thane of Cawdor, king hereafter
questions.hint: Macbeth already holds the first title.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What do the witches predict for Banquo?
options: His descendants will be kings, though he will not be
He will become Thane of Cawdor
questions.answer: His descendants will be kings, though he will not be
questions.hint: Think about the future of his family line.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why is the prediction about Banquo significant for a Jacobean audience?
options: King James was believed to be descended from Banquo
Banquo was the author of the play
Banquo was a real English king
questions.answer: King James was believed to be descended from Banquo
questions.hint: Think about flattering the king in the audience.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How does Banquo react to the witches compared with Macbeth?
options: He is more suspicious and warns that evil may tell truths to trick people
He is more excited and plans murder
questions.answer: He is more suspicious and warns that evil may tell truths to trick people
questions.hint: He calls them 'instruments of darkness'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: The witches often speak in rhyming lines with a strong, chant-like rhythm. What is the effect?
options: It makes their speech sound like spells, separating them from other characters
It makes them sound noble and royal
questions.answer: It makes their speech sound like spells, separating them from other characters
questions.hint: Compare their speech with the nobles' blank verse.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: To what extent are the witches responsible for Macbeth's actions? Refer to their prophecies in your answer.
questions.hint: Consider whether they force him or only suggest.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Explain how Shakespeare uses the witches to explore the Jacobean fear of the supernatural.
questions.hint: Link the context to specific moments in the play.
